title: Ship 0.1.3 with the evidence bar and transition rule

history.detail:
CONDITIONAL: CONDITIONAL — round 1. Audited 4d7ed29 (release content) + b1cc3c5 (bookkeeping). Sprint file re-read fresh immediately before this verdict.

REQUIREMENTS COVERAGE

Req 1 — MET. qa1.md step 4 states the demonstration standard (counterexample, reproduction, or command output; not a reading of the code alone) and cites sprint 1's path-encoding blocker with the re-derivation detail.

Req 1a — MET. The counterweight is in the same paragraph, not a separate section, and is bolded like the standard itself, so a skimming reader hits both. Reader test applied: someone who stops early still lands on "one confirmed defect is enough for a FAIL, and an accurate verdict is never held open waiting for evidence that cannot change it." The LiveQA stall is cited as the real precedent. CONDITIONAL is explicitly bound to the same rule.

Req 1b — MET. Explicit: "Authoring tests for your own findings is Dev Team's job, not yours; a demonstration can be a one-off repro script or command you throw away, it does not need to become part of the suite." Bounds it without weakening the standard.

Req 2 — MET. Rule is in CLAUDE.md immediately after the tree-hash section, credited to the external team, with the worked example. I verified the claim against the code rather than the sprint file's phrasing: sprint_lifecycle.py:478 does accept dev_agreed_done, and carries a comment saying it exists precisely so ship's tree-hash error is not a dead end. The documentation matches the mechanism.

Req 2a — MET, and strongly. "Read this as a constraint on how a precondition gets added, never as a reason not to add one... The rule is 'pair every gate with a recovery path,' not 'don't add gates.'" No reasonable agent comes away thinking gates are discouraged.

Req 3 — MET with one defect, see ISSUE 1 below. Convention is recorded with reasoning inline, and cmd_dev_done's real handling (sprint_lifecycle.py:513-522, state.get("qa1_audit_file_hash") plus the migration comment) is cited accurately.

Req 3a — MET. git diff 0fd7973..4d7ed29 -- scripts/ is empty. Did not re-run smoke_test.sh: with zero changes under scripts/ there is nothing for it to regress against, and the acceptance criterion is the diff, which I verified directly.

Req 4 — MET. package.json is 0.1.3; the diff to that file is exactly one line.

Req 5 — MET as written, with a finding the criterion did not anticipate, see ISSUE 2. I ran npm pack myself, extracted the tarball, and additionally installed it into a scratch directory. docs/sprints/ in both tarball and installed target contains only the seven .gitkeep placeholders. No registry.json, no state/*.json, no sprint markdown under any phase folder, no .claude/settings.local.json. Nothing sprint-related in the file list, so this is not the FAIL the criterion describes.

Req 6 — MET. 4d7ed29 touches exactly .claude/agents/qa1.md, CLAUDE.md, package.json (35 insertions, 2 deletions). Bookkeeping is correctly isolated in b1cc3c5. All four target commits confirmed ancestors of 4d7ed29 via git merge-base --is-ancestor: f2557d4 yes, 2238f44 yes, 192de1d yes, 0fd7973 yes.

ISSUE 1 — REQUIRED FIX (minor severity, but it is a defect in this sprint's own text)

CLAUDE.md, the new state-field access paragraph. The definition given is temporal and correct ("fields that have been in a sprint's state dict since it was first created"). The lookup shortcut offered in the parenthetical is not: "see cmd_start: id, phase, qa1_audit_result, audit_rounds, history, and the rest of that literal."

Demonstrated by reading cmd_start's literal at sprint_lifecycle.py:415-429. It contains fourteen keys today, and five of them are post-hoc additions: qa1_audit_file_hash, qa1_audited_tree_hash, last_shipped_commit, groundtruth_result, live_test_rounds. A reader who follows "the rest of that literal" indexes qa1_audit_file_hash directly and breaks cmd_dev_done's migration path.

That is not a hypothetical misread. It is the exact field the same paragraph holds up as the .get() precedent, so the paragraph's cited lookup method contradicts the paragraph's cited example. This is also precisely the failure Req 3a exists to prevent: someone "fixing" the .get() into direct indexing.

Fix is one line and touches no code. Either drop "and the rest of that literal", or qualify it: cmd_start's literal today also contains later additions like qa1_audit_file_hash, and the test is when a field was added, not whether it appears there now.

ISSUE 2 — NOT A FIX FOR THIS SPRINT. MASTER CONTROLLER SCOPE DECISION, NEEDED BEFORE PIPEMAN PUBLISHES.

Req 5a names the stake as this machine's home-directory paths and the real client project name "Licenseprofessor Edits and fixes", and calls it information disclosure. It assumes the only vector is the state files. It is not.

Demonstrated, not argued. I packed the real tarball, installed it into a clean scratch directory, and grepped the result:
  /tmp/fc-target/scripts/launcher/session.js:67 — "(`~/Programming/Licenseprofessor Edits and fixes`, seven such"
That is the client name plus the directory-count observation, verbatim, written into every installing project. scripts/launcher is FRAMEWORK_OWNED, so install.js copies it into every target and overwrites it on every upgrade. The tarball also carries scripts/launcher_test.js:128 with a hardcoded /Users/chrishobbs/... path.

This is the fail-open denylist Req 5 warns about, landing on a file nobody thought to look at. It is pre-existing, not introduced here: git log -S confirms it entered in 896cac3 (sprint 1's fix commit), so it already shipped in 0.1.2 and is already public. This release republishes it.

I am not making this a required fix, because fixing it inside this sprint would directly violate Req 3a's "git diff shows zero changes under scripts/" and Req 6's "nothing in scripts/ changes" — I would be demanding a change I then have to fail. The sprint file already says who owns that call: scope decisions are Master Controller's, not Dev Team's. It pairs naturally with the package.json files-allowlist item already deferred in Out of Scope.

Sequencing note: this CONDITIONAL returns the sprint to dev_build, which is a clean window for Master Controller to amend scope if it wants the comment rewritten. If the sprint file is amended, re-run /sprint-qa1 against the amended file — expected, not a bug.

ISSUE 3 — INFORMATIONAL, FOR PIPEMAN

npm pack packs the working tree, not the audited commit. .vscode/settings.json is currently modified and uncommitted (fullyCompletely.autoLaunch flipped false to true), and Out of Scope says leave it alone, so it will still be dirty at publish time. The packed tarball carries autoLaunch: true while the audited commit has false.

Verified inert this release: .vscode is not in FRAMEWORK_OWNED, and mergeSettings (install.js:311-327) hardcodes the value false and never reads the source file. Installing the tarball into a scratch target produced autoLaunch: false, as it should. So no action needed on this file — but the general gap is real. What ships is the working tree, and only the commit gets audited.

CODE QUALITY

Test coverage: none added, correctly. Documentation and a version string; Req 3a and Req 6 forbid touching scripts/. Existing suite is untouched and unaffected.
Error handling: n/a, no code paths changed.
Standards compliance: both CLAUDE.md additions are accurate against the code they describe. I re-derived both claims from the script rather than trusting the sprint file's phrasing, and both hold. Commit hygiene is right — content and bookkeeping split, which is what makes Req 6's check land cleanly.
Security: the tarball carries no sprint data. It does carry a client project name and a developer home path in source comments, see Issue 2.

RECOMMENDATION

Fix Issue 1 (one line in CLAUDE.md), re-run /sprint-qa1 3, then dev-done and ship. Master Controller should rule on Issue 2 before Pipeman publishes; if it amends the sprint file, that forces a re-audit, which is the check working as intended.
